edges.effect_quant: The adult-focused meta-analysis found improved attention and concentration with iron supplementation (SMD 0.59, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.90), with IQ gains in anaemic groups of about 2.5 points.
edges.population: older children and adults with low iron status, especially young menstruating women
edges.mechanism: Iron supports oxygen delivery, mitochondrial function, and neurotransmitter synthesis in brain networks involved in attention and working memory. When iron status is low, cognition often looks more vulnerable in speed and concentration domains than in broader global measures.
edges.summary: Iron supplementation appears to improve selected cognitive outcomes in iron-deplete people, particularly attention-related domains. The signal is not universal across every test battery, but systematic review and randomized evidence in young women point to a real if modest benefit when iron status improves.
edges.caveats: The literature is concentrated in young women and mixed-age trial pools, not in older adults with established neurodegenerative disease. Benefits also look more consistent for attention and working memory than for every memory or scholastic endpoint.

evidence.citation: Falkingham M et al 2010 Nutr J
